title: Navigable is never taken out of delaying load events mode if javascript: navigation does not create a document
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Consider a document containing an iframe with a normal http request that has a slow response.

Step 16 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate says the iframe's navigable should enter the delaying the load event mode when navigation begins. This stops when the headers for the response are received (in step 2 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#finalize-a-cross-document-navigation). If the headers are received but the navigation body is ongoing, then a new navigation is initiated to `javascript:undefined`, browsers ignore this second navigation because it does not result in a new document (#2590, tested by [javascript-url-abort-return-value-undefined.tentative.html](https://wpt.fyi/results/html/browsers/browsing-the-web/navigating-across-documents/javascript-url-abort/javascript-url-abort-return-value-undefined.tentative.html?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=html%2Fbrowsers%2Fbrowsing-the-web%2Fnavigating-across-documents%2Fjavascript-url-abort%2Fjavascript-url-abort-return-value-undefined.tentative.html)).

However, the process of starting the navigation to the javascript: URL passes through step 16 of the navigate algorithm again, which puts the navigable back in the delaying the load events mode. There is no cleanup step that takes the navigable out of this mode when no document results (see step 21 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate and 8.2 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate-to-a-javascript:-url). If browsers matched the spec, this would result in a page that never has a load event.
